title: That shooting star? It was a grain of sand 🌠
description:
Shooting stars aren't stars: most are crumbs of comet dust the size of a sand grain, hitting the air at up to 71 km/s and making it glow ~100 km up. The Leonids peak on 17-18 November 2026 (up to ~15 an hour).

Sources: Britannica on meteors; NASA on meteors and meteorites; Space.com on the 2026 Leonids.

meta.topic: shooting stars are sand-grain comet dust (speed, glow at ~100 km, Leonids 2026)
meta.idea_source: trending + viral: Leonids peak 17-18 Nov 2026 (Space.com); 'shooting stars are just sand' surprise

humour.trend: 'Remember November 2026' meme (revived on TikTok since late Aug 2026, peaking now it's November), as a side-eye + 'remember november 2026? it was sand' card

claims.claim: a typical visible meteor comes from a sand-grain-sized particle
shower meteors are comet debris (Leonids: comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle)
Leonids enter at ~71 km/s; London-Paris ~344 km = ~5 s
glow from heated, ionised air and vapour, starting ~100 km up
